messages:
alice: quick heads-up — saw a customer repro where Go SDK's SSE reader fails when a chunk splits inside a multibyte emoji inside a JSON string. it just hangs parsing partial JSON. anyone seen this?
kevin: ugh. which sdk version? any logs? stack trace?
alice: SDK v0.9.6. logs: "json: unexpected EOF" after a long pause. no panics. happens under high throughput + auth refresh spikes.
maria: we recently changed auth refresh to block the connection while rotating tokens for a sec — could be contributing to backpressure leading to fragmented chunks :thinking_face:
sam: i have a tiny repro. streaming endpoint sends NDJSON events and sometimes a single JSON object is split across packets at byte boundary for 4-byte emoji. Go's json.Unmarshal fails if you feed incomplete bytes.
sam: repro gist: ```go
r := bufio.NewReader(conn)
for {
  line, err := r.ReadBytes('
')
  if err != nil { break }
  // line may be partial if server emits without newline
  var ev map[string]interface{}
  if err := json.Unmarshal(line, &ev); err != nil {
    // currently we log and drop
  }
}
```
kevin: try using json.Decoder with Decode() on a buffered stream — but Decoder expects full objects too. alternative: accumulate bytes until you get a valid JSON boundary. i usually do incremental concat + try json.Unmarshal and only advance when success.
alice: any libs we can reuse? we want minimal allocation and robust handling across languages.
maria: for auth pause issue, can we make token refresh non-blocking? i.e., prefetch new token and swap quickly so reader isn't paused. that should reduce mid-object pauses.
sam: also consider handling multibyte boundaries: always treat input as UTF-8 stream and don't slice raw bytes into runes midway. Use bytes.Buffer and only attempt unmarshal when first and last non-space chars are { } or [ ] — cheap heuristic.
kevin: +1. another trick: require the server to emit newline after each event (NDJSON) — then r.ReadBytes('
') will get complete objects. but we can't change some third-party servers.
maria: for backpressure: implement a small read-window with adaptive sleep. e.g., after N parse errors in M secs, slow reads by 10ms and increase JV cache capacity. also add metrics: "partial_json_retries".
alice: here's a quick patch idea i pushed on the PR: attempt up to 3 incremental appends before marking an event as malformed, and record the size of the last chunk that fixed it. thoughts?
kevin: lgtm. can you add unit tests that simulate split at multibyte boundary? also add a test for auth-refresh pause causing stalled stream and ensure we don't leak goroutines.
sam: i'll add a small net.Pipe test and a fuzz test for random split positions.
ci-bot: CI: build passed for branch fix/stream-partial-json — tests 102/102 :white_check_mark: (link: https://ci.redwood/1234)
alice: sweet, thanks all. i'll update the PR with kevin's test suggestions and maria's metric. will also add a short note in the changelog about the auth non-blocking swap.
kevin: thanks — ping us when ready for review. :thumbsup:
maria: nice win!
